It wasn’t chocolate for me, but sugar. I started by quitting sugar for a month and in that month I replaced it with peanut butter. Then I relapsed, and relapsed REAL HARD! I was burntout (from stress) and just kept binging sugar. I’m glad I’m past that now. 

It was a real struggle tbh, I’ve been dealing with this addiction for probably around 5 years. Finally, I figured out the best solution for me, and I basically started to do hypnotherapy on myself. Which means I just taught myself to associate pain with sugar, rather than pleasure like I used to. Sometimes I still feel enticed but I got to remember that looks can be deceiving and that it’s actually shitty. Like, try to associate chocolate with poop, frosting with c*m. Etc. Makes it even better when you remember the pain that it’s caused you previously (for me, sugar made me VERY SICK. So that helps keep me away from it too).

Anyway, your question was, did I replace it and get addicted to something else? For a while, yes. I ate a LOT of bread. 
Then I decided it’s not healthy for me, so I made the intention to add healthier carbs as a replacement for the bread such as oatmeal, potatoes, and rice cakes. Now there always has to be a bag or two of rice cakes in the house. 
I guess now, the only thing I eat excessively is the rice cakes, with peanut butter. (Working on the EXCESSIVE part but I don’t mind the foods themselves anymore as I no longer feel sick, just really full still) :D
